title: Domestic vs Industrial Sewing Machines: Which Do You Need?
description: Domestic and industrial sewing machines compared: speed, stitch types, motors, space, noise and cost, so you can choose the right machine for home or business.
intro: Thinking of going industrial for a small business or a heavy hobby? Here is how the two worlds differ.

image.alt: Large room of blue industrial machines

cardText: Speed, stitch types, motors, space and cost compared.

sections.html: A domestic machine does many things reasonably well: straight stitch, zigzag, buttonholes, decorative stitches. An industrial machine usually does one job extremely well, all day, at high speed. That is why workrooms have separate lockstitch, overlock and coverstitch machines.
Industrial machines sew far faster than domestic ones. Modern servo motors make them controllable at low speeds too, which is why many home sewers now use them.
An industrial machine comes on its own table with a motor underneath. It needs floor space and is heavier to move. Servo models are much quieter than old clutch motors.

Industrial machines use their own needle systems (for example DBx1 for many lockstitch machines) and need regular oiling unless they are dry-head models. Parts are widely available through trade suppliers.
